en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Third Chapter
Discourse on Restraint:
Is there restraint among the devas?
Yes, [it is said].
Is there non-restraint among the devas?
One should not say so… [etc.
… Is there no non-restraint among the devas?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there no restraint among the devas?
You should not say so …pe… [and so on].
Is it not the case that non-restraint is non-virtue (asīla) and restraint is virtue (sīla), and that there is restraint among the devas?
Yes, it is so.
Is there then non-restraint among the devas, such that from that non-restraint restraint is virtue?
It should not be stated thus... [and so on]...
Understand the refutation.
If non-restraint were restraint and virtue, and if there is restraint among the devas, then indeed, O sir, you must admit this.
“There is non-restraint among the devas; from that non-restraint, restraint is virtue.
As for what you said there—“Indeed, it should be stated: — [it is as follows:]
"It is false to say: ‘Non-restraint is restraint; it is virtue; there is restraint among the devas,’ yet not to say:
‘There is non-restraint among the devas, from which restraint arises as virtue.
If, however, you cannot say this, [then your position is untenable].
“If it is said: ‘There is non-restraint among the devas; from that non-restraint, restraint is virtue,’ then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘Restraint is virtue arising from non-restraint, and there is restraint among the devas.
As for what you have stated therein—”
“If it must be said that ‘non-restraint is restraint, virtue; there is restraint among the devas,’ then it is false to say:
‘there is non-restraint among the devas, from which non-restraint restraint-virtue arises.
Is there restraint among humans, and is there non-restraint there?”
“Yes.
“Is there restraint among the devas, and is there non-restraint there?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
"There is restraint among the devas, but no lack of restraint there"?—
Yes. "There is restraint among human beings, but no lack of restraint there"?— [Is this also yes?]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there among the devas abstinence from taking life? Yes.
Is there the taking of life among the devas?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is there among the devas the abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there among the devas the use of fermented liquor, distilled liquor, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is there no killing of living beings among the devas? Yes.
Is there no abstention from killing of living beings among the devas?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is no fermented liquor, distilled spirits, or intoxicants causing negligence among the devas?
Yes, it is.
Is there among the devas the abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
One should not say so… [etc.
… Is there among humans the abstention from taking life, and yet is there taking life there?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there abstention from taking life among the devas, yet is there taking of life there?
You must not say so… [and so on]…

Among humans there is abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence; is there, however, fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence there [among humans]?
Yes.

Among the devas there is abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence; is there, however, fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence there [among the devas]?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there abstention from taking life among the devas, and is there no taking of life there? Yes.
Is there among humans the abstention from taking life, yet no taking of life exists there?

One should not say so… [and so on]… Is there among the devas the abstention from the occasion for negligence consisting of fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants, yet no such occasion for negligence consisting of fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants exists there?
“Yes.

“But is there among humans the abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence, yet no fermented liquor, spirits, or intoxicants which are the basis for negligence present there?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so forth].
"There is no restraint among the gods"?
Yes, you say.

Then are all the gods killers of living beings, takers of what is not given, indulgers in sexual misconduct, speakers of falsehood, and addicted to fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants that cause negligence?
It should not be stated thus...
[as before] ...therefore, there is restraint among the devas.
The Discussion on Restraint is finished.
